Farmhouse life

What is a farm stay? And why it beats a Rishikesh hotel

📅 6 Oct 2026·⏱ 6 min read·By Geetu
Home / Journal / What is a farm stay

People search "farm house in Rishikesh" and then ask us, slightly unsure: "So… what actually is a farm stay? Is it a hotel?" Fair question. Here's the honest version — including who it isn't for.

In one line: a farm stay is accommodation on a farm, where you stay close to the land, eat home-cooked meals from local produce, and live at a slower pace. It's smaller and more personal than a hotel — you trade uniform amenities for authenticity, quiet and real hospitality.

Farm stay, homestay, resort — what's the difference?

Farm stayHotel / resort
Run byA family, on-siteStaff & management
FoodHome-cooked, local, often all meals inMenu / buffet, à la carte
ScaleA handful of roomsDozens to hundreds
You getPlace, people, quiet, natureConsistency, amenities, service
Best forRest, families, slow travelBusiness, nightlife, large groups

Why a farm stay beats a hotel (for the right traveller)

The food is real. At a farm stay the kitchen cooks what the land and the season give — in our case, three Garhwali meals a day, mostly vegetarian, often from the garden. You can't buy that at a buffet. The pace is different. No lobby, no check-in queue, no corridor of identical doors — just forest, a terrace, and mornings that start with birdsong instead of traffic. And the welcome is personal. A hotel remembers your room number; a farm stay remembers your name.

Let's be honest about the trade-offs

A farm stay is not for everyone, and we'd rather you know that before you book. You won't find a swimming pool, 24-hour room service, or a nightclub. The nearest big market is a drive away. If your idea of a holiday is amenities and buzz, a town hotel will serve you better — and we'll happily say so.

What a farm stay in Rishikesh looks like with us

At JuneGiri, a farm stay means a forest-view room, three home-cooked meals, and direct access to the trails and the river — all at the edge of Rajaji National Park. It's the same impulse behind our Stay Pass: for people who fall in love with this kind of travel and want to keep coming back. If that sounds like your kind of holiday, the plan your stay page has everything — rates, what's included, and how to book in two minutes.

You don't check in to a farm stay. You arrive, you exhale, and somewhere around the second morning you stop checking your phone. That's the whole point.
